record.file_problem: Full text is present; the authors state that experimental verification is omitted.
record.tranche_reason: Derives theoretical results about how gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent change the train–test generalization gap, using gradient means and covariance rather than empirical architecture or optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: The study reports theoretical formulas and arguments, not measured model outcomes. The introduction's statements about models and SGD performance cite other work and are not rows. No rows for cited empirical findings.
record.test_reason: The paper derives local, leading-order GD/SGD update formulas, but none tests a specified claim version. In particular, it does not establish V5's held-out performance comparison across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets. Experimental verification is explicitly deferred.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors derive a leading-order expected single-update loss-gap increase proportional to gradient-covariance trace divided by training-set size, and interpret the expected difference between successive SGD and GD updates as implicit regularization through decorrelation. They acknowledge higher-order and train/test-gradient-distribution corrections and defer experimental verification.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical derivation of generalization-gap changes under GD and SGD; no empirical training recipe or model comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The derived gap change depends on learning rate, training-set size, and gradient covariance; the authors also describe an additional term when train and test gradient distributions diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Equation (9) derives an expected single-update increase in the loss generalization gap of learning rate times gradient-covariance trace divided by training-set size, to leading order. Section 4 adds a correction when training and test gradient distributions differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the derivation's assumptions, local expected generalization-gap growth depends on gradient covariance, learning rate, and training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3, equations (10)–(13), compares two full-batch GD updates with two non-overlapping half-batch SGD updates and interprets their expected gradient difference as implicit regularization of the local gap change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: To leading order, decorrelation between successive minibatches introduces an implicit regularization term relative to repeated full-batch updates.

record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Workshop on Integration of Deep Learning Theories; arXiv version dated 2021
record.problems: No experimental verification is reported. The analysis is a leading-order expansion in learning rate and inverse batch or dataset size; the authors note omitted higher-order corrections and that train and test gradient distributions can diverge during overfitting.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows: the paper reports theoretical derivations, and its empirical generalization statements are cited prior work or explicitly omitted experiments.

Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.

record.verdict_notes: No rows require correction. The absence of experiments alone does not exclude a theoretical test; the decisive issue is that these local update results do not establish or refute any supplied version. The introductory empirical claims and sharpness discussion rely on prior work.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization experiments.
